name: AROS claim flow zeroed its own AMM pair reserve
summary: AROS's signed claims pay out of its own AROS/USDT pair and then sync it, with no floor on the remaining reserve. The attacker bought the pair down to its claimable amount, routing the AROS to the whitelisted feeRecipient to pass the buy block, claimed that amount so sync set the AROS reserve to zero, and bought all the pair's USDT for a little AROS.
notes: Reset is setLPPair (slot 0x1f8), the latest change the exploit needed: the claims drain and sync lpPair. It follows the proxy's creation with implementation 0xd948279f and the whitelisting of feeRecipient, which let the buy pass the R1 hook. The per-tx and daily claim caps raised later only bound claim size, and tradingRestricted is a gate.

Victim depletion is the AROS/USDT pair's USDT, at par; the attacker's purchase leg and flash-loan principals net out and fees are not deducted. The 622,117,209 AROS also drained, mostly to feeRecipient, is left unvalued because the transaction destroyed the token's only market.
The 38 earlier pair-to-feeRecipient buys were sent by the feeRecipient Safe itself; no other transaction exercised the drain before the exploit.
